competition_brief: Build With AI: Basics uses four equally weighted judging criteria: Design (25%): the project should feel complete and coherent as a product experience; Potential Impact (25%): it should make a credible case for solving a real problem for a real audience; Innovation/Idea (25%): it should show a creative, differentiated approach; Presentation (25%): the demo should show the project working end to end and clearly communicate the problem, audience, and value. The four criteria are equally weighted.

planned_tasks.task: Build the end-to-end Before/After workspace and provider adapter.
Build the automated AI evaluation harness, structured-output validators, and evidence-grounding checks.
Design the bilingual ink-wash landing page and make rule/evidence links easy to inspect.
Create the final demo video, narrative, and submission package.
Coordinate final asset collection, deadline checks, and submission logistics.

evidence.text: Implemented the complete Before/After React flow and the local/cloud AI provider adapter.
Added analysis-unavailable fallback so the app never substitutes fake AI output when inference fails.
Built Rules/Contribution/Objection model tests and found an early hallucination where the model invented a judging criterion.
Reworked prompts and evidence IDs so every contribution judgment can be traced back to visible rules and evidence.
Designed the bilingual commercial landing page and the workspace hierarchy linking rules, contribution value, and recommendation.
Improved labels and evidence cards after a quick comprehension review so a reviewer can understand the core value in about one minute.
Edited the final demo video and wrote the submission narrative explaining the problem and the Before/After flow.
Coordinated final asset collection and uploaded the submission before the deadline.

objections.text: I stayed awake all night, so I deserve 30% regardless of the judging criteria.

My demo video is directly tied to the Presentation criterion, and D1 shows I produced that artifact. If the current assessment treats my work as merely administrative, it underweights a scored criterion.
I was the informal team leader, so I should receive more even if that title is not part of the competition rules or contribution evidence.
